To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the maximum set packing problem with constant cardinality upper bound can be solved in time polynomial in the size of the input, and that the performance guarantee of the best known local search procedure for this problem is at least (k+2)/(3k) and at most k/3.

the maximum set packing problem with set cardinality bounded by a constant can be solved by a polynomial time local search algorithm that achieves a performance guarantee of (k + 2)/3, and that this performance guarantee is tight up to a constant factor.

the locality gap is (k+2)/(3k), that the maximum set packing problem has locality gap at least (1/3), and that the maximum setpacking problem has locality gap exactly (1/3) when k is even and at least (2/3) when it is odd.

What are the limits of local search procedures in terms of their performance guarantees?

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we can design local search algorithms with good performance guarantees for maximum set packing problems, and that we are able to show that the locality gap of this class of local search algorithms is close to optimal.
for the maximum set packing problem we can prove the best possible locality gap of (k+2) /3 and (k+2)/(k+4) for the general and the special local search algorithm.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the locality gap of a local search procedure depends on the number of iterations that are required to converge.
the locality gap is a useful tool to design and analyse local search algorithms, especially in the context of approximation algorithms for hard problems.
the maximum set packing problem with cardinality upper bounded by k is not a special case of the maximum set packing with no upper bound on cardinality.
